A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPS/LS-DPS research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and retained content can be matched across reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original defense experiments across six attack datasets, MM-Vet evaluations, ablations, runtime measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen2.5-VL-32B evaluations, further comparator experiments, crop-count sensitivity, and statistical results.

M1.justification: The partial-image responses, supervision of the full-image model, safety-awareness prompts, and optional LLM safety checker remain unchanged. V2's additional adaptive-cropping implementation description does not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use RTA-100, Self-Gen, MultiTrust, MM-SafetyBench, HADES, VisualAttack, and MM-Vet. The added experiments reuse this coverage; adding Qwen2.5-VL-32B changes the evaluated model configuration, not the datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds the random-cropping Standard comparator to Tables 1–2, enhanced voting variants of Protector, IVA, Warning, and ECSO in Table 5, and comparisons against five purification methods and MirrorCheck in Tables 11–13. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds Qwen2.5-VL-32B evaluation, seven-query majority-vote baseline controls, a one-to-five random-crop sweep, and test-data threshold optimization for MirrorCheck. These introduce substantive additional protocols; the original attack filtering, evaluator models, and main cropping settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses examine whether additional baseline queries explain the defense advantage, sensitivity to crop count, and a Warning Prompt meme-understanding case (Table 5, Table 7, Figure 7). The earlier crop-strategy, safety-awareness, and multi-agent debate analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without statistical uncertainty. V2 introduces ± values for Qwen2.5-VL-32B results and t-tests against the best baseline, reporting p-values of 0.02–0.04 in Table 10. The meaning of ±, run counts, and seeds remain unspecified.

E6.justification: The original benchmark and ablation table values are retained, but substantial new results are added. For example, Table 8 reports Qwen2.5-VL-32B DPS ASRs of 0.22, 0.35, and 0.16 on the three misleading datasets. Reported LS-DPS runtime changes from 81 to 72.2 seconds, without sufficient setting information to establish a comparable speedup.

T1.justification: New Appendix C introduces an output-probability formulation and crop-text consistency reweighting in Equations 3–6. Section 3.2 also defines confidence through inverse response standard deviation. These formalizations are absent from v1, although the asserted clean-output probability advantage is not proved from stated conditions.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a black-box, training-free defense using partial perceptions, effectiveness against misleading and jailbreak attacks, and preservation of standard performance. The abstract retains the same 76.3% average ASR reduction across six datasets and three models.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the added query controls as supporting the computational tradeoff and attributes MirrorCheck's lower standard performance to false positives. Limitations now emphasize attacks surviving cropping and possible detection-based combinations; v1's explicit exclusion of nonvisual attacks is no longer stated.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access URL, a Qwen2.5-VL-32B model link, and identifies GPT-4o-Mini text-box localization and cropping of remaining regions as an adaptive-cropping implementation detail. Most existing prompts, crop sizes, and evaluation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Related work expands to include VLMGuard, MirrorCheck, naturalistic patch attacks, and additional adversarial-purification literature. Appendix D.6 contrasts purification and detection approaches with DPS, while the original weak-to-strong and multi-agent positioning remains.

P1.justification: V2 clarifies inference-time supervision, replaces persuasion terminology with confidence, moves v1 Appendix A into Section 3.3, and incorporates limitations into the conclusion. Appendices and author information are reorganized, but most existing prose and the main methodological narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different conference layout and single-column appendices, expands the main tables with Standard columns, and adds numerous experimental tables and Figures 6–7. V1's fuller appendix Figure 5 becomes the main Figure 2, replacing the shorter illustration; this is relocated evidence.

improvement.justification: The added cropping comparator, extra-query controls, and open-source evaluation make the empirical evidence more informative; code-access and implementation disclosures also help. Benefits are tempered by unspecified uncertainty/run details and Appendix C's unsupported probability ordering. The retained 2.5-times-best-baseline claim is also unreconciled with Table 1's stronger Standard comparator: Qwen-VL-Plus ASR 0.48 versus DPS 0.31.
